text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging: Elevated 5xx and streaming disconnects detected (gateway -> runtime). Severity: P1. Root cause unknown. Alert: spike in 502/504 and TLS early EOFs on streaming endpoints. Current metric: streaming error rate 12% (baseline 0.8%). First seen 2529008600. Please acknowledge and stand up live mitigation.

oncall-sre: acked. I'm on it. grabbing logs and tracing.

eng-runtime: I'm also joining — will check gateway -> runtime handoff and kernel OOMs. sending profiler.

alice: quick note — customer A reported degraded streaming earlier this morning, might be related. @oncall-sre can you correlate request IDs?

oncall-sre: pulling traces now. sample span: gateway->proxy->runtime. seeing a lot of `chunked` streams that stop mid-frame and client cancel signals. possible abrupt client resets or runtime process side closes.

bob: I see a pattern: gateway returns 502 when runtime sends RST_STREAM or partial chunk then closes. suspect connection-level resets rather than application error.

eng-runtime: checking runtime logs: pattern of `write: broken pipe` and `kv cache miss` spikes. no obvious OOMs on the nodes. attaching snippet:

```
2026-03-15T10:52:10Z runtime-7f8f   ERROR  stream_writer.go:214 write failed: broken pipe
2026-03-15T10:52:10Z runtime-7f8f   WARN   conn.go:98 keepalive timeout for client 10.2.5.21
```

lina: gateway metrics show concurrent connections spiking in one region (us-west-2). Could be a bad client causing head-of-line blocking.

sean: customer impact calc: approx 15% of streaming sessions get truncated — mostly long-running streams (>30s). non-stream endpoints not affected.

oncall-sre: mitigation idea 1: enable paged fallback for streaming endpoints (switch long polls to paged) to reduce long-lived connections and avoid gateway backpressure. Anyone want to own a quick config?

eng-runtime: I can roll a config change to enable paged fallback at the gateway for the affected route group. Will do a canary in us-west-2 then region-wide if green.

alice: mitigation idea 2: increase gateway keepalive timeout and soften connection backoff so transient resets don't immediately surface as 5xx. Might reduce client cancel noise while we root cause.

bob: also suggest temporary rate-limit on a tenant if we see a single client hammering long streams. But need a safe threshold.

oncall-sre: action list so far:
- eng-runtime: enable paged fallback canary now (owner)
- alice: bump gateway keepalive from 30s -> 60s in us-west-2 canary (owner)
- bob: monitor per-client connection rates + set soft limit (owner)
- oncall-sre: customer impact notice + triage doc + escalate to infra if node-level network flaps seen (owner)

eng-runtime: canary config applied to 10% of traffic for streaming-route alpha. monitoring. rolling back if errors increase.

30s later...

eng-runtime: canary looks promising: stream error rate in canary shard down from 13% -> 2.2%. latencies stable.

oncall-sre: rolling canary to 50% now.

alice: gateway keepalive increased on the canary cluster. seeing fewer early EOFs but still occasional client resets.

bob: flagged one client IP (203.0.113.42) with 8k concurrent streams; throttling applied and reduced error tail. likely a misbehaving SDK.

sean: customer impact updated: after mitigations, affected sessions dropped to ~3% globally. SLA risk window reduced.

incident-bot: :white_check_mark: Mitigation applied: paged fallback + keepalive bump + per-client soft throttling. Please prepare handoff notes for next on-call.

oncall-sre: Handoff summary for next shift (copy into incident channel):
- Issue: intermittent streaming disconnects and 5xx (502/504) caused by connection resets and long-lived streams hitting gateway/router backpressure.
- Impact: up to 15% of streaming sessions truncated at peak, now reduced to ~3% after mitigations. Customers affected: Customer A (investigating), multiple smaller tenants.
- Actions taken: Enabled paged fallback canary -> rolled region-wide, increased gateway keepalive (30s->60s) for canary then region, soft per-client throttling on abusive IPs, escalated to infra to monitor NIC errors.
- Evidence: runtime logs show `broken pipe` and keepalive timeouts; gateway metrics exhibit head-of-line long-connection spikes; identified one high fanout client IP.
- Next steps for next oncall: 1) Continue monitor for regressions for 4h, 2) Engage SDK team for client behavior (message framing / reconnect strategy), 3) If errors spike after rollback of paged fallback, pause rollbacks and escalate to runtime owners.
- Runbook commands used: `kubectl -n prod rollout restart deploy/gateway-usw2` (canary), `curl -v -N https://gateway.redwood.example/streaming-route | sed -n '1,100p'` to reproduce partial frames.

lina: leaving note: infra NIC metrics show increased retransmits on a single host; infra will rotate that host tomorrow at 02:00 UTC.

alice: adding follow-up: we should add a synthetic long-stream test to CI that simulates sudden client cancels to catch regressions early. Filing ticket ENG-5123.

eng-runtime: logging more context on streaming writer errors (request_id, shard id). will ship in next patch.

oncall-sre: closing live mitigation — incident is in monitoring mode. handing off to oncall for the rest of shift. If anyone sees >5% error rate re-alert.

sean: confirmed. thanks team. will update customer A and post postmortem draft if we need a full blameless write-up.

oncall-sre: end of thread — handoff to tomorrow's oncall. All actions documented above. :lock:
